title: The Locked Cell Lab
story: You and NOVA are in the biology lab when the door jams. NOVA is learning to recognise cells with a microscope camera, but it keeps getting them wrong. Teach it, check it and fix it to open four locks.
escaped: The lab door clicks open. NOVA now looks for real differences between cells and knows not to judge everything from a few samples.

locks.title: Plant cell or animal cell?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort cells into plant cells and animal cells. Choose the clues it should look at, then test it on two new cells.
locks.hint: Onion peel cells are plant cells, but they aren't green. And every cell here has a nucleus.
locks.learn: 'Looks green' fitted every plant cell NOVA was shown, but onion cells aren't green. The real differences, a cell wall and a large vacuole, sort every cell. An AI is only as good as the clues it uses.

locks.title: Check NOVA's claim about big animals
locks.intro: NOVA explains why elephants are big. Is it right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: Elephants are bigger than ants because their cells are much bigger.
evidence: The size of cells has no relation to the size of the body; an elephant's cells are not necessarily bigger than a rat's.
Some organisms are made of just one cell.
A nerve cell is long and branched.
Cells were first seen by Robert Hooke.
locks.hint: What does the textbook say about cell size and body size?
locks.learn: A guess that sounds logical can still be wrong. Bigger animals have MORE cells, not bigger ones. Evidence beats a confident guess.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's cell-part jobs
locks.intro: NOVA has matched cell parts to their jobs. Tick the matches that are wrong.

rows.label: Separates the cell from its surroundings and lets materials in and out
Controls the activities of the cell
Carries genes from parents to offspring
rows.why: genes are on the chromosomes in the nucleus

rows.label: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
rows.why: that is the cell membrane's job

locks.hint: Where are genes found? Which part decides what goes in and out?
locks.learn: Mixed-up labels teach an AI mixed-up facts. Fixing the data is often better than building a cleverer AI.

locks.title: Is all pond life single-celled?
locks.intro: NOVA looked at three drops of pond water under a microscope.
locks.question: NOVA says: 'Every living thing in the pond is single-celled.' What is the honest conclusion?
options: NOVA is right: all three samples agree.
These drops had single-celled organisms, but fish, frogs and pond plants are multicellular. Three drops can't speak for everything in the pond.
Microscopes can only see single cells.
locks.hint: What else lives in a pond that wouldn't fit in a drop of water?
locks.learn: An AI trained on a small or one-sided sample makes wide claims that are wrong. Ask: what did the data leave out?
